jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Research Compute Services
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM Research Compute Services builds the systems that help researchers use OpenAI’s compute fleet effectively. We partner with Research and Compute Infrastructure to support workloads across the compute stack, including pretraining, synthetic data generation, sampling, research inference, and reinforcement learning. Our work connects changing research needs with capacity planning, allocation, and scheduling. We build tools and services that help researchers express their compute needs, access the right resources, and run their workloads effectively. As the fleet and our research ambitions grow, we continually improve how compute is planned, allocated, and used. ABOUT THE ROLE You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, partnering closely with the Research Compute Services team. Your primary responsibility will be to build and own the tools, data, and platform that turn Research plans and workload signals into concrete compute demand and manage allocations across the fleet. This is a hands-on technical role. You will build alongside researchers and engineers, working directly with code and data to prototype solutions, automate workflows, and deliver tools that teams use every day. You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable. You will work across a broad range of Research workloads, understanding their different requirements and ensuring those needs shape the platform. Success means researchers can express their needs, understand their allocations, and use compute effectively as priorities and workloads change. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Build with Research. Work directly with researchers across pretraining, research inference, and other workloads. Treat these communities as core users, and translate their needs into improvements across compute services, tooling, and scheduling. - Own Research demand and allocation systems. Own the roadmap and delivery of the tools, data, and platform used to capture demand, support allocation decisions, and manage allocations. Carry this work from requirements and design through adoption and ongoing improvement. - Turn research plans into actionable demand. Develop systems that translate evolving plans and workload requirements into concrete capacity needs, including resource requirements, timing, and constraints. - Connect capacity supply and demand. Partner with Capacity Planning, Research, and infrastructure teams to reconcile demand with available supply. Build the tools and workflows needed to evaluate scenarios, manage changes, and make allocation tradeoffs visible to decision makers. - Build reliable data and useful tools. Create data models, views, and automation that show what researchers need, what capacity is available, what has been allocated, and how it is being used. Improve self-service workflows for requesting and managing compute. - Connect allocations to workload execution. Partner with engineers working on Kubernetes deployments and scheduling systems so allocation plans reflect workload constraints and translate into resources that researchers can use. - Improve allocation and scheduling efficiency. Work with engineers to evaluate optimization approaches, including solvers operating at fleet and local scheduling levels. Help define constraints and objectives, assess tradeoffs, and measure improvements in fleet utilization. - Find and address systemic gaps. Use workload and fleet data to identify bottlenecks, unused capacity, and recurring manual work. Build durable improvements to the tools and systems behind those problems. - Lead technical delivery across teams. Own plans, dependencies, and decisions across Research, Research Compute Services, Capacity Planning, and infrastructure engineering. Keep teams aligned on what needs to be built, how it will be adopted, and who will operate it. - Make progress and tradeoffs clear. Give working teams and leadership a clear view of demand, allocation constraints, delivery progress, and decisions that need attention. jobs.title: Process Value Engineer
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary The BP&T Process Value Engineer is responsible for identifying, shaping, and accelerating process improvement and value realization opportunities across Global Supply Chain operations. The role sits within the Hyderabad BP&T organization and acts as a specialist capability focused on process excellence, process engineering, process intelligence, simulation, and automation enablement. Working closely with Global Supply Chain capability owners, process excellence teams, business SMEs, BIT, data, analytics, digital adoption, and automation teams, the role converts process knowledge into actionable improvement opportunities. This includes leveraging ADONIS and other process intelligence capabilities to analyze process performance, identify bottlenecks and non-value-added work, model current and future states, simulate improvement scenarios, and prioritize opportunities that unlock measurable value. The ideal candidate combines strong process engineering discipline with digital fluency, analytical thinking, business partnering, and a value-led mindset. This individual must be comfortable working across global teams and helping the business move from process documentation to process intelligence, optimization, and automation at scale. Duties/Responsibilities • Identify, assess, and prioritize process improvement opportunities across Global Supply Chain operations, with a focus on simplification, standardization, automation, cycle time reduction, risk reduction, and measurable business value. • Use ADONIS and process intelligence capabilities to analyze current-state and future-state process maps, process hierarchies, RACI structures, systems, data flows, risks, controls, cycle times, handoffs, and operating pain points. • Translate process models and operational insights into value cases, improvement hypotheses, clear recommendations, and leadership-ready decision support. • Lead process engineering analysis to identify bottlenecks, rework, manual tasks, duplicate activities, compliance risks, decision delays, and non-value-added activities across end-to-end supply chain processes. • Develop and apply value assessment frameworks, including effort-vs-impact analysis, benefit sizing, feasibility assessment, readiness criteria, and prioritization logic for process improvement, automation, and AI-enabled opportunities. • Leverage process simulation and scenario analysis to compare current and future-state options, quantify value drivers, and support business cases for change. • Partner with process owners, capability leads, operational SMEs, and digital teams to convert process opportunities into prioritized backlogs, delivery roadmaps, and implementation plans. • Support process automation opportunity identification by highlighting manual, repeatable, rules-based, high-volume, or exception-driven activities that may be suitable for workflow automation, low-code automation, AI agents, or other digital solutions. • Develop reusable templates, methods, and playbooks for process value assessment, process mining/readiness reviews, automation candidate identification, and process intelligence reporting. • Build process performance dashboards and value realization views that connect process metrics, adoption measures, quality indicators, operational KPIs, and improvement outcomes. • Strengthen process governance by supporting reviews of process accuracy, metadata completeness, ownership, readiness for automation, and alignment with approved BPM standards and lifecycle controls. • Facilitate workshops and working sessions with business teams to validate pain points, capture improvement opportunities, align on future-state design, and secure cross-functional ownership of actions. • Partner with BIT, analytics, data, digital adoption, and AI enablement teams to ensure improvement opportunities are aligned with enterprise technology standards, data readiness, governance, and scalable solution design. • Support change management, adoption, training, and communications activities to ensure process improvements are understood, embedded, measured, and sustained across global teams. • Stay current on leading practices in process excellence, process mining, process intelligence, simulation, automation, AI-enabled process transformation, and supply chain operating model innovation, incorporating relevant practices into GSC capabilities and roadmaps. Reporting Relationship This position reports to the Senior Director, Hyderabad, Business Performance & Transformation, Global Supply Chain. Qualifications Education: • B.S. or BA in Engineering, Supply Chain, Business, Information Systems, Data Analytics, Operations Management, or a related discipline; a Masters or MBA preferred. • Operational excellence, Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, process mining, BPM, or value engineering certification preferred. Experience: • 5+ years of experience in process excellence, process engineering, business process management, supply chain operations, operational excellence, digital transformation, business analysis, or related disciplines; life sciences or pharmaceutical experience preferred. • Demonstrated experience analyzing end-to-end business processes and identifying opportunities for simplification, standardization, optimization, automation, and measurable value creation. • Strong understanding of BPM methods, process hierarchy, process modeling standards, governance workflows, operating model design, RACI, SIPOC, value stream thinking, and continuous improvement practices. • Experience with BPMN 2.0 and enterprise process management platforms such as ADONIS, ARIS, Signavio, or equivalent tools. • Familiarity with process intelligence, process mining, process simulation, workflow automation, analytics, AI-enabled process improvement, and digital adoption capabilities is strongly preferred. • Ability to structure business cases and quantify value using process metrics, cycle times, cost drivers, service levels, productivity indicators, risk indicators, and operational KPIs. • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to connect process, data, systems, people, controls, and business outcomes into practical improvement recommendations. • Strong stakeholder management and facilitation skills, with the ability to lead workshops, challenge constructively, influence without authority, and communicate complex ideas in a clear and business-focused way. • Experience supporting transformation initiatives in complex, matrixed, global environments across multiple functions, geographies, and time zones. • Understanding of regulated environments, compliance expectations, quality systems, process controls, documentation standards, and audit readiness is preferred. Additional professional and personal requirements include: • Strong value-led mindset with an ability to move process work beyond documentation into measurable performance improvement, optimization, and adoption. • Ability to work independently in a fast-paced environment, balancing structured analysis, stakeholder engagement, and hands-on execution. • Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to create concise, leadership-ready summaries, roadmaps, and recommendations. Dear Bristol Myers Squibb Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Process Value Engineer opportunity with Bristol Myers Squibb at Bristol Myers Squibb.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: Internal Communications Manager, Product
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Anthropic is seeking an Internal Communications Manager to serve as a dedicated communications partner to our Product organization. Internal communications at Anthropic is not a support function that plans meetings and sends newsletters. The best people in this role operate like advisors who embed themselves deeply in the orgs they support, earn a seat at the leadership table, write on behalf of executives, and see around corners, anticipating what the organization will need to hear before anyone asks for it. There are traditional elements to the role too, like all-hands planning and org change announcements, and you'll run those with operational excellence. But the heart of the job is more creative and will require you to find ways to connect the rest of the company to some of the most consequential and least visible work at Anthropic, and making the line between that work and our mission clear and strong. Product is the bridge between what our models can do and what our customers’ needs today. Capabilities are improving constantly, and priorities shift as the models improve, and launches can come together very quickly as a result. For much of the company, it can be hard to keep up with what's shipping, what's changing, and why it matters. Your job is to help people make sense of that pace by understanding the work, and the people doing it, well enough to tell its story credibly, and to help its leaders communicate with clarity and candor as the company scales. Responsibilities Own the internal communications strategy for your portfolio, becoming an expert in the team's work and a trusted member of its leadership team Serve as a hands-on advisor to executives - help them think through what to say and when, draft communications in their voice, and give them honest counsel, especially in moments when that’s challenging or uncomfortable. Translate deeply technical work into narratives that land with employees across every function, without losing the substance Get creative about how you connect people to the work - don't default to creating a slide deck when a demo or something no one has tried yet would land better Anticipate communications needs before they arrive (e.g. launches, incidents, organizational change, moments of external attention) and have a plan ready for how we’ll bring employees along Design and implement strategies to boost signal and reduce noise, so employees know what's important and what it means for them Plan and execute internal fora like all-hands and AMAs with operational excellence Exercise sound judgment with sensitive material, especially where security work requires care about what is shared, with whom, and when Partner closely with the broader internal communications team to ensure updates are accurately and consistently cascaded across existing channels and live forums You may be a good fit if you Have 8–12 years of experience in communications or an adjacent craft where you learned to make complex, high-stakes material clear under pressure (e.g journalism, speechwriting, chief of staff work, strategy and operations) Are an exceptional writer with a particular talent for distilling technical decisions and cross-functional projects into simple, compelling narratives, and can write convincingly in someone else's voice Have served as a trusted advisor to senior leaders and know how to build those relationships: when to push, when to listen, and how to deliver a recommendation even when it’s something an exec may not want to hear Can embed credibly with engineers, PMs, and researchers. You are curious about how technical systems work, ask good questions, and earn the trust of people who may be skeptical of comms by default See the big picture and are able to connect individual team updates to company strategy and mission Have a keen eye for organizational culture and can recognize authentic moments worth amplifying Strong candidates may also Have experience communicating about product ,engineering, security, infrastructure, or other technical domains Have worked at AI companies, frontier tech companies, or other organizations where the technical work moves faster than most people can follow Have built or run internal communications programs during periods of rapid organizational growth The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $265,000 — $295,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sr Associate - Commercial Analytics & AI Enablement (Data Scientist) opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

Best,
Celina Lin

These will be the models that detect cancer in the minimal residual disease (MRD) setting and help inform treatment selection. The ideal candidate brings a strong background in algorithm development, genomics, sequencing data processing, and applied machine learning. Primary Responsibilities: Develop, train, and evaluate machine learning models, driving algorithm design decisions that support cancer detection in the MRD setting. Own end-to-end research analyses, from ideation through implementation (scripts and notebooks), troubleshooting, and performance evaluation, including developing new features within existing pipelines. Translate between wet-lab experimental design and computational analysis, navigating ambiguity as assay requirements evolve and maintaining rigorous quality control across high-volume sequencing data spanning multiple cohorts, vendors, and clinical protocols. Communicate findings and model performance to both technical and cross-functional stakeholders, and contribute to establishing standards for code quality and reproducibility. Qualifications: PhD in Computer Science, Bioinformatics, Computational Biology, or a related quantitative field with a strong emphasis on cancer epi/genomics and 4 to 8+ years of experience post-PhD. Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities: Deep theoretical and practical understanding of high-throughput DNA sequence data analysis, including mapping, sequence alignment, and variant calling workflows. Experience in algorithm development and data analysis, including applying and evaluating statistical methods. Demonstrated experience in developing core ML models, including generalized linear models, kernel methods, tree-based algorithms, and neural networks, with a focus on biological data (e.g., DNA sequencing data) Strong quantitative reasoning and data analysis skills, with a demonstrated ability to apply them effectively to relevant scientific problems. Experience with Python and Linux command-line tools, including writing shell scripts. Strong computational and programming skills, including thorough experience with Python statistical packages (NumPy, Matplotlib, Pandas). Familiarity with public databases such as TCGA, COSMIC, or OncoKB. Ability to visualize findings and summarize results in oral and written form for both technical and non-technical audiences. High scientific rigor, with eagerness to teach and learn new computational methods and biology. Ability to work on a cross-functional team in a highly collaborative environment, partnering with both computational and experimental scientists. Final compensation will vary based on experience, qualifications, and internal equity considerations. Our aim is to make personalized genetic testing and diagnostics part of the standard of care to protect health and enable earlier and more targeted interventions that lead to longer, healthier lives. The Natera team consists of highly dedicated statisticians, geneticists, doctors, laboratory scientists, business professionals, software engineers and many other professionals from world-class institutions, who care deeply for our work and each other. Other benefits include pregnancy and baby bonding leave, 401k benefits, commuter benefits and much more. We also offer a generous employee referral program! We are committed to ensuring a diverse and inclusive workplace environment, and welcome people of different backgrounds, experiences, abilities and perspectives. Inclusive collaboration benefits our employees, our community and our patients, and is critical to our mission of changing the management of disease worldwide. Link: https://www.natera.com/notice-of-data-collection-california-residents/ Please be advised that Natera will reach out to candidates with a @ natera.com email domain ONLY. Amgen is advancing a broad and deep pipeline of medicines to treat cancer, heart disease, inflammatory conditions, rare diseases and obesity and obesity-related conditions. As a member of the Amgen team, you’ll help make a lasting impact on the lives of patients as we research, manufacture, and deliver innovative medicines to help people live longer, fuller happier lives. Our award-winning culture is collaborative, innovative, and science based. If you have a passion for challenges and the opportunities that lie within them, you’ll thrive as part of the Amgen team. Join us and transform the lives of patients while transforming your career. Manager Channel Analytics & Operations What you will do As a key member of the Channel Analytics and Operations team within US Value & Access (USV&A), the Channel Analytics Manager validates and analyzes wholesaler inventory and sales data, maintains wholesaler accounts, and supports accurate execution of channel processes. The role works closely with wholesalers, third-party vendors, lead analysts, and cross-functional partners to resolve data issues, support distribution fee payments and price actions, and maintain compliant, reliable reporting. This role will also aid in the project management of product launch activities across Contracts & Pricing Execution (CPE) Key responsiblities · Validate wholesaler data — Perform daily validation and reconciliation of wholesaler inventory and sales submissions, including EDI 852 and EDI 867 data, and compare results with Amgen ex-factory sales and other relevant sources. · Resolve discrepancies and improve data quality — Work with wholesalers, third-party vendors, lead Channel analysts, and internal partners to investigate data issues, correct account or submission errors, reduce recurring discrepancies, and strengthen data integrity. · Maintain wholesaler accounts and contract data — Implement account and contract changes, monitor changes for operational feasibility, and support process updates needed to keep channel operations accurate and current. · Support wholesaler fee payments — Prepare, validate, and reconcile data used in quarterly wholesaler distribution fee payments; support monthly payment activities when applicable and ensure calculations are complete and accurate. · Support product launches — Assist in product launch project management ensuring seamless execution of product launch activities across CPE. · Maintain compliant operations — Follow applicable operational guidelines, government pricing sub-certification requirements, Sarbanes-Oxley controls, and other relevant policies. Support required reconciliations, reporting, and documentation. · Analyze and communicate results — Translate high-volume data and analysis into clear summaries, presentations, and recommendations that help team management and business partners make informed decisions. · Improve processes and systems — Identify opportunities to improve QA/QC methods, reporting, and operational processes. Collaborate with IT/IS to document requirements, investigate system defects, and support enhancements and process efficiencies. · Coordinate projects and partnerships — Participate in planned and ad hoc projects across Channel Management and Contract Operations. Build effective working relationships with segment teams, Trade, Pricing, Government Pricing, Finance, IS, vendors, and wholesalers. Preferred Qualifications: · Experience in pharma/biotech with an emphasis in analytics and operations · Excellent communication skills, including building and delivering presentations and translating complex data/processes into clear, concise summaries across multiple systems · Strong strategic thinking and problem-solving: synthesizes information, navigates ambiguity, and enables actionable business analysis · Supervisory/people-management experience and demonstrated growth in responsibility and leadership · Strong financial acumen/background · Proven ability to lead multiple complex projects concurrently through completion · Effective collaborator in fast-paced, fluid, cross-functional, matrixed environments · High attention to detail and reporting accuracy while maintaining strong conceptual focus · Identifies and implements cross-functional process improvement opportunities · Applies sound judgment to support organization structure What you can expect from us As we work to develop treatments that take care of others, we also work to care for your professional and personal growth and well-being. cold_email.subject: Interest in Associate Strategic Planning & Operations — biology/bioinformatics graduate
cold_email.body:
Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Associate Strategic Planning & Operations opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in building scalable data systems that let research and clinical teams use biological data reliably. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, I have built API-driven and Snakemake-based pipelines, automated SQL workflows, and worked across both scientific and software contexts.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin

jobs.title: MES Engineer IT Systems
jobs.description: At Bristol Myers Squibb, our employees often ask, “Who are you working for?”—a question that fuels collaboration, accountability, and urgency in our work. Our purpose-driven culture inspires us to discover, develop, and deliver innovative medicines to prevail over serious diseases. We offer uniquely interesting and meaningful work, opportunities for growth, and a supportive environment that values inclusion, wellbeing, flexibility, and comprehensive benefits. This is work that transforms the lives of patients, and the careers of those who do it. Position Summary: The MES Product Owner for Breyanzi is accountable for the end-to-end Manufacturing Execution System (MES) solution supporting the Breyanzi (CAR T cell therapy) manufacturing process at BMS, Bothell. This individual serves as the process and product expert who translates Manufacturing, Quality and Supply Chain requirements into clear, buildable specifications for MES engineers, leads a sub-team that includes junior and offshore engineers, and ensures that the resulting electronic batch records (EBRs) are compliant, efficient and inspection-ready. The role also acts as the sprint manager for the Breyanzi book of work, leading Agile delivery in Jira and reporting project status to stakeholders. The role requires hands-on MES experience (Syncade preferred), ownership of production deviations and CAPAs related to Breyanzi, and participation in the on-call rotation for L2 escalations. Must ensure GMP-regulated documentation processes and procedures are in place for all activities to meet quality and compliance standards. The candidate should have at least 5 years of experience in pharma/biotech, with specific expertise in Manufacturing, Quality, and Supply Chain systems and in Computer System Validation (CSV). Hands-on Breyanzi process knowledge is a strong advantage, and eMES development experience will stand out. Strong analytical, problem-solving, and communication skills are required. Key Responsibilities: Product Ownership – Breyanzi MES Act as Product Owner for Breyanzi from an MES standpoint: own the product backlog, prioritize enhancements and fixes, and maintain the roadmap in alignment with Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Facilities and Tech Transfer stakeholders. Serve as the Breyanzi process subject matter expert for MES; capture and document detailed requirements and translate them into User Requirements, Functional and Design Specifications and test cases. Bridge the gap between process requirements and engineering build, ensuring requirements are fully translated into complete EBRs in MES that meet GMP compliance and regulatory expectations (including 21 CFR Part 11 and data integrity principles). Sprint and Project Management Lead Agile sprints in Jira for the Breyanzi book of work in a role similar to sprint manager, including sprint planning, backlog grooming, user story review and approval, sprint reviews and retrospectives. Maintain the project plan, including milestones, timelines, dependencies, risks and issues, and keep it current as scope and priorities change. Create and publish high-level project scorecards and status reports for IT and business leadership, covering progress against milestones, risks, and delivery health. Team Leadership, Review and Training Lead the Breyanzi MES sub-team, including offshore resources who may be early in their careers; assign work, set expectations, and track delivery. Review design, configuration and test work performed by developers; provide guidance and feedback on quality, optimizations and enhancements to EBRs and MES recipes/workflows. Train and onboard new engineers on the Breyanzi manufacturing process and MES build standards to build team capability and reduce reliance on individuals. Operations, Quality and Compliance Fully accountable for addressing production deviations and CAPA actions related to Breyanzi MES, including investigation, root cause analysis, corrective/preventive implementation and effectiveness checks. Provide primary application support for Breyanzi MES and serve on the on-call rotation to support L2 escalations for production issues. Maintain the validated state of the system through the change control process – creating changes in ServiceNow, obtaining pre-approval, executing/deploying changes, attaching evidence, closing tasks and obtaining post-approval. Participate in GMP validation activities including development and execution of IQ/OQ/PQ testing, and support software releases, audits and inspections. Identify and drive process and system improvements, standardization and reuse across Breyanzi EBRs and other manufacturing systems. Qualifications & Experience: Required Experience/Education Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Life Sciences, Computer Science or related field, or equivalent experience 5+ years of relevant industry experience in biopharmaceutical/cell therapy manufacturing and/or manufacturing IT systems Strong working knowledge of the Breyanzi manufacturing process (or comparable autologous cell therapy process) Hands-on experience with Manufacturing Execution Systems, preferably Syncade, including EBR design and build Experience leading or mentoring engineers, including offshore or junior team members, and translating business requirements into technical specifications Experience managing production deviations, investigations and CAPAs in a GMP environment Experience with electronic document management and quality management systems, and with change control and CSV/validation practices in regulated industries Technical writing competency and GMP procedure writing Strong communication, collaboration and stakeholder management skills Willingness to participate in on-call rotation for L2 production support Preferred Experience Prior experience developing in eMES Prior experience supporting commercial CAR T cell therapy manufacturing Experience with 21 CFR Part 11, GAMP 5 and data integrity requirements We hire for skills and capabilities, not just credentials – if this role excites you, but doesn’t perfectly match your resume, we encourage you to apply anyway. Compensation Overview: Bothell - WA - US: $108,650 - $131,655 The starting pay range(s) listed above is for full-time employees (FTE). You may also be eligible for additional discretionary incentive cash and stock opportunities. We determine starting pay thoughtfully – carefully considering the nature of the role, required skills, work location, schedule and the knowledge and experience you bring. Final compensation is guided by pay equity principles and applicable employment laws. Compensation programs are reviewed on an ongoing basis and may be adjusted over time to reflect evolving market factors, and individual, team or Company performance. Benefits: Subject to the terms and conditions of the applicable plans then in effect, you may be eligible to participate in our comprehensive benefit plans – including wellbeing support, retirement and financial protection benefits, and insurance offerings (medical, dental, vision, life and disability). U.S.-based exempt employees are eligible for Flexible Time Off (FTO), which provides paid time off without a set accrual limit, subject to manager approval, along with 11 paid company holidays each year. Non-exempt employees, RayzeBio employees, and employees located in Puerto Rico receive 160 hours of paid vacation annually for new hires (subject to manager approval), 11 paid company holidays, and 3 optional holidays. Depending on eligibility, employees may also have access to additional time-off benefits, including paid sick leave, up to two paid volunteer days per year, summer hours flexibility, and leaves of absence for medical, personal, parental, caregiver, bereavement, or military needs. Eligible employees also enjoy an annual Global Shutdown between Christmas Day and New Year's Day. Learn more at https://careers.bms.com/ways-of-working. jobs.title: Manager, Account Manager | Growth
jobs.description: ABOUT RAMP Ramp is building the smart infrastructure for finance teams, embedded in the transaction flow of every dollar a business spends. We automate how over $275B in annualized spend flows in and out of 85,000+ companies: authorizing payments, flagging risk, categorizing spend, and closing books. The problems are high-stakes, data-dense, and unforgiving. We hire people with high agency and high urgency. We look for slope over intercept. We care less about where you trained and more about what you’ve built. At Ramp, everyone is a builder who owns problems end to end and makes consequential decisions that shape the outcome. The median Ramp customer saves 7.5% and grows revenue 16% in their first year – far in excess of businesses operating without Ramp. We believe every ambitious company deserves the same. If you want to build systems that directly shape how companies move and manage billions, Ramp is the place to do it. About The Role The next chapter of Ramp's growth runs straight through the customers we already have: 80,000+ finance teams who adopted us for one thing and haven't yet seen what the rest of the platform can do for them. Account Management owns that opportunity - and this role owns the team building the motion to capture it. You'll lead a group of 5-8 Account Managers, each carrying a book of ~3,000 emerging and SMB customers with real latitude over how they grow it. This is a build role, not a maintain role: the playbooks, coaching systems, and performance bar you set are the ones this team runs on next year. Your ceiling is set by how well you turn individual AM judgment into a repeatable, scalable motion that grows the segment. What You’ll Do - Build and run a high-performing team of 5-8 Account Managers - setting the bar for culture, morale, and daily execution. - Understand where to prioritize your teams time. Engage directly with AMs to identify and break into top accounts, especially where trust is being built or repaired. - Own the number. Manage quota performance and pipeline generation across your team to hit spend activation, product activation, retention, and expansion goals. Forecast your business to senior leadership on a weekly cadence. - Hire and develop the next generation of AMs - training on product, buyer personas, competition, and tooling through role-plays, game film, and real deal work. - Coach relentlessly. Run daily 1:1s, dissect call feedback, lead enablement sessions, and build career paths for every rep on your team. - Turn what works into a system. Continuously refine team processes and tooling to improve output and efficiency as the segment scales. - Represent Account Management cross-functionally, partnering with Sales, CX, CSM, Risk, and Product to remove blockers and drive outcomes. What You’ll Need - Minimum 2+ years of quota-carrying sales or account management experience as an individual contributor, with a proven, consistent track record of exceeding goals (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory) - Minimum 1+ years building and leading account management or sales teams, with a track record of exceeding goal (new business or cross-sell/upsell experience mandatory) - Prior success in fast-paced, results-oriented GTM environments, ideally at SaaS or AI companies - A genuine passion for hiring, with a thoughtful approach to team planning and development - Ability to articulate contractual, technical, and financial value to customers, including executive leaders - Proficiency with data analytics tools (Salesforce, Looker, Excel) and a bias toward using data to drive decisions - Strong collaboration and influencing skills, backed by excellent communication and presentation ability - High agency and adaptability - no two days are the same, and the only constant is change - A desire and willingness to jump headfirst into complex, challenging problems for the good of the business. jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Capacity Analytics & Tooling
jobs.description: ABOUT THE TEAM The Compute Infrastructure team runs the GPU fleet and large-scale compute clusters that serve the models backing ChatGPT and the API, while also supporting training workloads for our next generation models. We operate a large, modern GPU fleet and provide a unified platform for other OpenAI teams to run production Applied AI and Research training workloads. We seek to learn from deployment and distribute the benefits of AI, while ensuring that this powerful tool is used responsibly and safely. Safety is more important to us than unfettered growth. ABOUT THE ROLE You will join the Compute Infrastructure TPM team as a Technical Program Manager for Capacity Analytics & Tooling. You will serve as the product manager for our supply and demand planning tools, owning the strategy, roadmap, and delivery of the systems teams use to forecast demand, understand supply, and plan allocations. Your users will include Product TPMs, Capacity TPMs, and Compute TPMs, alongside partners across Finance, Accounting, Leadership, Engineering, and Research. This role combines product management, technical program leadership, data engineering, and applied data science. You will partner with engineering and data teams to build reliable data foundations, improve forecasting and scenario planning, and scale our tools and success metrics across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. You will help teams make informed capacity decisions across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other infrastructure providers. This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees. IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL: - Own the product strategy and roadmap for supply and demand planning tools. Understand user needs, set priorities, define success measures, and guide delivery from initial requirements through adoption and ongoing improvement. - Build useful planning workflows. Translate complex processes into tools for demand intake, forecasting, supply tracking, scenario analysis, and allocation planning. Help teams understand what infrastructure they need, when it will be available, and which gaps require action. - Scale the data infrastructure behind capacity planning. Partner with engineering on ingestion, transformation, storage, and delivery of planning data. Guide technical tradeoffs as the number of resources, providers, data sources, and users grows. - Make planning data consistent and trustworthy. Establish shared data models and definitions for supply, demand, allocations, utilization, and cost. Drive data cleaning, validation, reconciliation, and traceability so users can understand and trust planning outputs. - Advance forecasting and analytical capabilities. Work with engineering and data partners to connect product and research plans to infrastructure demand. Make assumptions, uncertainty, forecast accuracy, and capacity constraints visible to decision makers. - Define and scale meaningful success metrics. Measure data quality, forecast performance, planning speed, and tool adoption. Establish consistent ways to track capacity availability, utilization, and efficiency across CPU, storage, network, and GPU resources. - Support planning across multiple cloud providers. Build capabilities that account for differences in resource types, regions, availability, commercial commitments, and deployment constraints across AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI, and other providers. - Lead delivery across data, infrastructure, and planning teams. Manage dependencies, technical tradeoffs, migrations, risks, and releases. Keep teams aligned on priorities and the decisions needed to move work forward. - Drive adoption and reduce manual planning work. Develop simple workflows, documentation, training, and feedback mechanisms. Identify recurring reconciliation and reporting work that can be improved through better data and automation. - Make capacity tradeoffs clear to leadership and partner teams. Provide useful views of gaps between supply and demand, allocation options, and their financial and operational consequences. Partner with Finance and Accounting to align planning data with budgeting and reporting needs. YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU: - Have 5+ years of experience leading technical programs or products in data platforms, infrastructure, capacity planning, or a related field, with a record of delivering systems that teams rely on. - Have owned an internal product or platform roadmap and translated complex operational needs into requirements, priorities, and releases that users adopt. - Have direct experience with capacity planning, including demand forecasting, supply planning, allocations, and resource constraints. You understand how utilization, performance, availability, and cost affect planning decisions. - Understand modern data infrastructure, including ingestion, transformation, batch and streaming processing, and analytical storage. You have worked with technologies such as Fivetran, dbt, Spark, Kafka, or comparable systems and can discuss their architectural tradeoffs. - Have practical experience with data modeling, data cleaning, validation, and reconciliation. You can use SQL and Python or similar tools to investigate discrepancies, validate assumptions, and prototype analyses. - Have applied quantitative methods to forecasting, scenario analysis, or optimization. You can assess model assumptions and uncertainty, evaluate forecast performance, and explain the limitations of an analysis. - Understand the capacity, performance, and cost characteristics of compute, storage, networking, and accelerators. You have experience working across multiple cloud environments and can account for differences between providers. - Can lead complex programs with many technical dependencies and align teams with different priorities. You communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to engineers, researchers, finance partners, and leaders. - Are resourceful in ambiguous environments, exercise sound product judgment, and build simple, scalable ways to solve complex planning problems. - Are interested in and thoughtful about the impacts of AGI. My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Staff Integration Engineer opportunity with Illumina at Illumina.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. In my independent BRCA1/BRCA2 project, I built a reproducible Python and Snakemake workflow using BCFtools and ANNOVAR to analyze population-specific variants and examine discrepancies between clinical labels and observed allele frequencies. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

The combination of rigorous biological questions, collaborative research, and hands-on computational work in this role is exactly the environment in which I hope to grow. I would be grateful for a 15–20 minute conversation to learn more about the lab's current priorities and discuss where my background could be useful. I have attached my resume for context.

Best,
Celina Lin
https://linkedin.com/in/celina-g-lin

jobs.title: BIM Designer & Coordinator: Civil
jobs.description: About the Team Industrial Compute develops the infrastructure that powers OpenAI’s AI systems. Our Design organization connects engineering, construction, and digital delivery to support complex data center campuses from initial planning through deployment. Working with internal teams, design consultants, and construction partners, we develop coordinated designs that address site constraints, infrastructure requirements, and future growth. Our BIM team provides the models and workflows needed to deliver consistently across the portfolio. About the Role We are seeking a hands-on Civil BIM Designer & Coordinator with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience to support the planning and design of large-scale, mission-critical data center campuses and associated power generation, energy storage, and utility facilities. In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain civil models using Civil 3D and AutoCAD. Your scope will include site layouts, grading, drainage, roads, and utilities, coordinating buildings with generating equipment, battery energy storage systems (BESS), water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, substations, and cooling systems. You will work closely with civil engineers, BIM team, discipline designers, equipment vendors, and delivery partners to turn engineering requirements into clear models and deliverables. Your work will support early design reviews, resolve site coordination challenges, and establish repeatable civil BIM practices across concurrent projects. Detailed engineering requirements and specialist analyses will be provided by the responsible engineers. We are looking for a hands-on civil specialist who can independently manage modeling assignments, communicate design dependencies, and maintain quality as projects evolve. Key Responsibilities - Advance feasibility, constructability, and phasing: Prepare layout, grading, routing, and earthwork options for early design reviews; incorporate noise, exhaust dispersion, heat-rejection, safety, and environmental constraints. Model heavy-equipment delivery routes, turning movements, crane areas, laydown, maintenance clearances, staged construction, temporary-to-permanent generation transitions, and future expansion. - Lead civil site development: Create and maintain surfaces, grading and earthwork models, equipment and building pads, roads, alignments, profiles, and corridors. Incorporate flood protection, stormwater management, and containment or separation process-drainage requirements. - Develop and coordinate plant utility systems: Model gravity and pressure networks for gas supply, cooling and process water, fire water, wastewater, electrical duct banks, and communications. Coordinate utility models, routes, corridors, crossings, connections, and clearances with engineers, consultants, utility providers, vendors, and construction partners. - Integrate campus and power-generation infrastructure: Coordinate civil models with buildings, power plants, BESS, substations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, cooling systems, and other site utilities. Support simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas turbine, reciprocating engine, and CHP layouts while incorporating equipment separation, service access, and fire access. - Coordinate equipment, foundation, and thermal interfaces: Integrate vendor general arrangements, foundation footprints, equipment elevations, trenches, pits, and pipe-support locations with inputs from structural, geotechnical, mechanical, and electrical engineers. Coordinate civil interfaces for heat-recovery steam generators, steam-turbine facilities, heat exchangers, cooling towers, air-cooled condensers, radiator arrays, and thermal-distribution corridors. - Govern civil model data and multidisciplinary alignment: Manage Civil 3D data shortcuts, external references, coordinate systems, styles, templates, and parts libraries. Coordinate Civil 3D, Revit, vendor, and combined-discipline models; verify coordinates, origins, elevations, units, orientation, and model alignment in Navisworks. - Drive coordination and quality: Lead model reviews, investigate clashes and spatial conflicts, communicate design changes, and track issues through resolution. Review civil models and drawings for completeness, reference integrity, consistency, and compliance with project BIM requirements. - Deliver and improve civil BIM: Prepare plans, profiles, sections, model exports, review packages, and model-based quantities appropriate to each project phase. Maintain reusable content, document workflows, and improve delivery across data center, power-generation, energy-storage, and utility projects. Qualifications - Minimum 8 years of civil design, BIM modeling, or civil infrastructure drafting experience, plus a relevant degree/diploma or equivalent practical experience. - Experience supporting mission-critical facilities or complex industrial infrastructure across multiple disciplines. - Advanced Civil 3D and AutoCAD proficiency, including grading, corridors, utility networks, sheet production, data shortcuts, references, coordinate systems, and model dependencies. - Experience with site-survey data, GIS, point clouds, NavVis or similar laser-scanning/reality-capture workflows. - Experience with Navisworks, Revizto, and Autodesk Forma for model coordination, issue tracking, and markups. - Ability to independently deliver civil packages, interpret engineering and vendor information, identify missing inputs, and escalate engineering decisions appropriately. - Strong communication and organizational skills across changing priorities and concurrent projects. Preferred Skills - Direct experience with hyperscale, colocation, or other mission-critical data center campuses, from conceptual site planning through detailed design and construction coordination. - Experience supporting civil design and model coordination for one or more of the following: gas turbine or reciprocating engine power plants, combined-cycle or CHP facilities, BESS installations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, or comparable industrial infrastructure. - Familiarity with OEM installation requirements, equipment and foundation interfaces, maintenance envelopes, and balance-of-plant infrastructure. - Familiarity with Revit-to-Civil 3D workflows, including building locations, elevations, utility interfaces, and phased campus development. - Experience with GIS, survey data, point clouds, and civil data exchange workflows. - Experience reviewing consultant models, BIM execution plans, levels of development, model quality, and common data environments. - Experience improving production through Dynamo, scripting, or other automation tools. - For candidates with deeper experience, the ability to guide complex civil modeling packages, mentor colleagues, and improve shared standards. Your work enables coordinated delivery of data center campuses and associated power, energy storage, and utility infrastructure across the portfolio. jobs.title: Scaled Account Manager, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.location: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Nonprofits, universities and other mission-driven organizations do some of the hardest work in the world, usually with small teams and little technical capacity. As a Scaled Account Manager in Beneficial Deployments, you will be the person a named book of these organizations can rely on. You will own each customer relationship after the first conversation, including commercials, activation and the conversations that turn a new deployment into everyday use. This role sits on the Scaled Sales team within Beneficial Deployments, the part of Anthropic that brings Claude to mission-driven organizations sooner and further than the market would on its own. You will work with little to no dedicated Customer Success support, so you are both the seller and the person who helps a customer get real value. That is only possible if you work differently. You will use Claude to take on the short-horizon tasks that consume a book like this, and spend your time on strategic conversations. The role will also change. As we automate more of this work, the book will take less of your time, and that time moves to growth: deeper work with your highest-potential accounts, launches, events and programs that reach many more organizations. We are hiring someone who wants that: someone who will automate parts of their own job and move on to the next hard problem. What you'll do Own a named book of nonprofit and education customers. Take over existing relationships and run them end to end: retention, seat growth, plan moves and new contacts inside each organization. Drive activation yourself. Help priority customers in the segment go from purchased seats to weekly use, starting with where staff lose the most time: fundraising, grant writing, reporting and program operations at nonprofits, or research support, teaching and administration in higher ed. Automate your own work. Use Claude to handle account research, follow-ups, usage reviews and routine questions, then share what works so the whole team can use it. Spend your time on strategic conversations. Work with executive directors, operations leads, and IT and academic leaders at universities to find the use cases that matter to their mission and agree what success looks like. Spot who is ready for more. Identify customers moving from individual productivity toward redesigned workflows, build the case, and bring in Applied AI or other specialists when they qualify for deeper support. Build programs, not one-offs. When ten customers have the same problem, create a playbook, webinar or cohort that solves it once. Be the voice of your book. Bring what you hear to Product, Marketing, Support and Operations, and work across those teams to get customer problems fixed. Where your time goes as we automate The role starts mostly account-facing. Over roughly the first six months, we expect Claude to take on much of the routine work, and your time shifts toward growth. Examples of where it goes: Deeper with priority accounts. Spend real time with the 10 to 15% of your book that can move from individual productivity to redesigned workflows, and get them there. Quarterly launches. Beneficial Deployments brings new offerings to the nonprofit and education community each quarter. Help drive them: coordinate across Marketing, Comms and partner teams, and make sure your customers benefit. Events. Help shape and run the events, local and eventually international, that become a core part of how we reach new organizations. New signups and scaled partnerships. Contribute to the motions that bring new organizations onto Claude, including partner channels and programs for segments we don't yet serve well. The exact mix will change, and you will help decide it. Part of the job is working out which tasks should be automated and which still deserve a person's time. You may be a good fit if you have 3+ years of account management or customer success experience with nonprofit or higher education customers, with a proven track record of growing retention and driving adoption of new technology Have owned customer relationships in an account management or customer success role, and can point to accounts you grew, retained or turned around Use AI in your own work today, and can show a workflow you built that gave you real time back Bring structure to unfamiliar problems, and can move from a messy situation to a clear plan quickly Have run multi-step programs or projects with several stakeholders and kept them on track Have got things done through people you did not manage, across teams in a larger organization Stay effective when your job changes, and would see automating part of your role as a win Can explain AI plainly to people who are skeptical, busy or new to it Care about the mission of nonprofits and educational institutions, and about AI being developed and deployed safely Strong candidates may also Have built something from zero, such as a company, a product, a sales motion or a new program, or been an early employee at a startup Have a consulting background, with experience across many sectors and problem types Have worked at an AI-native company or sold AI products, or moved from business development into owning accounts Have worked in or with nonprofits, foundations, Universities or other mission-driven organizations Understand how nonprofits and universities buy, including boards, funders, procurement cycles and tight budgets Have used usage data to prioritize a large book of accounts The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $222,800 — $290,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Dear Amgen Hiring Team,

My name is Celina Lin, and I recently completed my Honours Bachelor of Science in Biology/Bioinformatics at the University of Waterloo. I am reaching out about the Sr Associate Commercial Analytics opportunity with Amgen at Amgen.

I am especially interested in the team's use of quantitative and computational methods to answer meaningful biological questions. I also completed two bioinformatics internships at the Ontario Institute for Cancer Research, where I developed an LLM-assisted competency-mapping pipeline and created research-data-management learning resources. More broadly, my background in biology, bioinformatics, Python, R, SQL, Linux, and reproducible workflow development aligns well with that kind of cross-disciplinary work.

Best,
Celina Lin

You will also lead programs that turn incoming supply into usable compute. Working across cloud providers, Data Center Infrastructure, and compute engineering teams, you will connect physical site readiness with the CPU, storage, network, GPU, and foundational services required to bring new sites and clusters online. You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, managing a broad portfolio of infrastructure programs and making dependencies, risks, and decisions clear from working teams through leadership. jobs.title: Applied Scientist, Engineering
jobs.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role The Discovery team at Anthropic is organized around the north star goal of building an AI scientist – a system capable of solving the long-term reasoning challenges and basic capabilities necessary to push the scientific and technological frontier. We're expanding our work on engineering and the applied sciences. Our goal is to contribute to training Claude to invent, design, and engineer across every discipline and scale, reliably and safely: new manufacturing and experimental techniques, processes, materials, devices, instruments, machines, energy systems, and factories. We want this work to accelerate science and technology and benefit people widely. We're seeking exceptional researchers with deep expertise in one or more of these areas. In this role, you'll work at the intersection of frontier AI and your field, developing rigorous methods to measure and improve Claude's performance on complex engineering and scientific tasks. You'll collaborate closely with researchers, engineers, and partners across Anthropic and industry to build AI systems that can engage in all phases of research and development, and to test Claude's designs against real-world feedback. Key responsibilities Design and implement evaluation methodologies for assessing AI model capabilities relevant to engineering and applied science research and applications Design realistic tasks and training environments, and curate data from your field Develop and validate simulations and computational tools for your field, and calibrate them against real-world data Work with industry partners, manufacturers, and labs to build and test what Claude invents, designs, and engineers, and bring that real-world feedback into evaluation and training Think through how Claude's engineering capabilities can permeate the real world: where they can have the most impact across industry and research, and what it takes to get them adopted Advise the team on which problems, tools, and workflows matter most in your field Collaborate with domain experts and partners to establish benchmarks and gather high-quality data for training Translate between engineering domain knowledge and machine learning objectives Minimum qualifications Deep expertise and hands-on R&D or industry experience in an engineering or applied science discipline, such as mechanical, electrical, materials, chemical, aerospace, structural, industrial, or manufacturing engineering; applied physics; computational simulation Experience with AI or machine learning, whether evaluating and training AI systems or applying these tools in your field Track record of taking work from concept through to a working result, such as a product, process, device, experiment, or tool Hands-on proficiency with the computational design, analysis, or simulation tools used in your field Basic programming proficiency, for example in Python Ability to navigate ambiguity and develop solutions in a rapidly evolving research environment Ability to work independently while collaborating closely with cross-functional teams, and to explain your field clearly to people outside it Commitment to using AI to accelerate engineering and scientific progress while maintaining high ethical standards Preferred qualifications 5+ years of hands-on R&D or industry experience in an engineering or applied science discipline Ph.D. in an engineering or applied science field, or equivalent industry experience Industry experience in product design and manufacturing, or in developing engineering or scientific simulation software Breadth across more than one discipline, or across several stages of the path from design to production Familiarity with modern AI model training methods Track record of building high-fidelity solvers or simulation engines that were validated against real-world data and used in practice Experience working with manufacturers, vendors, contract research organizations, or academic labs Experience managing data pipelines and working with large-scale technical datasets Publications, patents, or contributions to open-source scientific or engineering software The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU - Are a strong software engineer who can design reliable data pipelines, evaluation infrastructure, and internal tools. - Understand information retrieval concepts and metrics, while recognizing where conventional search metrics may not capture the quality of an AI-generated learning experience. - Have experience working with human-labeled data, relevance judgments, annotation programs, or model-based evaluation. - Are comfortable going deep into qualitative and quantitative data to identify subtle issues and systemic patterns. - Can turn ambiguous product goals—such as trustworthiness or educational usefulness—into clear, testable definitions of quality. - Communicate technical findings clearly and can influence decisions across research, engineering, product, and nontechnical partners. - Have a strong intrinsic desire to learn, fill gaps in your knowledge, and share what you discover with others. - Care deeply about building AI systems that help people learn while remaining accurate, responsible, and worthy of trust. NICE TO HAVE - Experience evaluating large language models, retrieval-augmented generation systems, or agentic search products. - Familiarity with learning science, education technology, assessment design, or educational measurement. - Experience with causal inference, online experimentation, or analysis of large-scale product telemetry. - Knowledge of evaluation challenges involving multilingual, multimodal, or age-appropriate learning experiences. - Experience developing or validating LLM-based graders and other automated evaluation methods.
